description: We are TAREEQ, a team of students passionate about technology, science, and space exploration. We are developing Martian Map, an interactive 3D platform for exploring Mars using NASA scientific data, terrain analysis, and intelligent route planning. We welcome creative and motivated participants interested in Python, AI/ML, data science, software development, 3D visualization, and space exploration.
summary: TAREEQ is an interactive Mars-mapping and route-planning prototype for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. It brings global 3D context together with a 2D map where users can inspect map layers, measure point-to-point distances, choose start and destination points, and compare Greedy, Uniform-Cost Search, and A* route options using elevation and slope costs. For the Jezero study area, TAREEQ uses a 20 m CTX digital terrain model and its matching 6 m orthophoto; elsewhere, it uses global MOLA topography at much coarser resolution. The goal is to make route trade-offs and their data sources easier to understand before a Mars surface excursion. This is a research prototype, not a certified navigation or rover-scale hazard-avoidance system.
details:
TAREEQ

Explore Mars. Understand Its Terrain. Navigate Beyond Earth.

The Problem

Exploring Mars is not simply about reaching a destination. It is about understanding the environment before attempting to navigate it.

The Martian surface is complex and diverse, containing steep slopes, craters, rocky formations, and potentially hazardous terrain.

Although NASA and other space agencies provide valuable scientific datasets about Mars, understanding and combining these datasets can be challenging.

Explorers need more than a map showing where places are. They need a way to understand the terrain, identify potential hazards, evaluate different routes, and make informed navigation decisions.

The challenge is turning complex Martian geospatial data into an understandable and interactive exploration experience.

Our Solution — TAREEQ

TAREEQ is an interactive Martian exploration and navigation platform designed to transform scientific Mars datasets into an immersive and understandable experience.

The platform combines a Mission Control Dashboard with an interactive 3D Martian environment, allowing users to explore a selected region of Mars, investigate its terrain, and plan routes between two locations.

Instead of presenting scientific data as isolated maps and measurements, VYRA brings different geospatial layers together in one unified environment.

Users can select a starting point and a destination, analyze the surrounding terrain, and compare multiple navigation alternatives based on distance, terrain difficulty, and potential risks.

Our goal is to make Martian exploration more visual, accessible, and data-driven.

Core Features

1. Mission Control Dashboard

A centralized interface that provides access to the exploration environment, mission information, terrain data, and navigation tools.

2. Immersive 3D Martian Terrain

An interactive three-dimensional representation of a selected Martian region, allowing users to zoom, rotate, and explore the surface.

3. Multi-Layer Geospatial Visualization

VYRA integrates five complementary layers:

  • Surface Imagery: Visual representation of the Martian surface.
  • Elevation: Terrain height and topographic variations.
  • Slope: Identification of steep and potentially difficult terrain.
  • Hazard: Representation of potential navigation obstacles.
  • Scientific Interest: Locations and regions with scientific exploration value.

4. Interactive Location Selection

Users can select their starting point and destination directly on the map using their mouse.

5. Intelligent Route Planning

VYRA uses the A* search algorithm and a terrain-based Cost Grid to calculate and compare three navigation alternatives:

  • Shortest Route: Prioritizes minimum travel distance.
  • Balanced Route: Balances distance and terrain difficulty.
  • Lowest-Risk Route: Prioritizes lower estimated navigation risk.

The result is a more informed approach to exploring the Martian surface.


Scientific Data & NASA Sources

VYRA is designed around real planetary geospatial datasets, with a focus on combining different sources of Martian surface information.

Our data exploration and integration workflow focuses on:

1. MOLA — Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter
Provides global elevation measurements that help us understand the large-scale topography of Mars.

2. CTX — Context Camera
Provides surface imagery that helps visualize Martian geological features and regional terrain characteristics.

3. HiRISE — High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment
Provides high-resolution orbital imagery and terrain products for detailed regional exploration.

4. HRSC — High Resolution Stereo Camera
Provides topographic and imaging products useful for analyzing Martian surface structures.

5. THEMIS — Thermal Emission Imaging System
Provides thermal and visible imaging data that contribute to geological and surface characterization.

Data Processing

Our geospatial workflow is designed to:

  • Inspect and validate raster datasets.
  • Check spatial reference systems (CRS).
  • Verify spatial resolution and coverage.
  • Process elevation data into terrain representations.
  • Derive slope information from elevation models.
  • Integrate geospatial layers into a unified navigation environment.

We distinguish between verified scientific observations, derived terrain indicators, and simulated data used for development and demonstration.

Technology Stack

VYRA combines modern web development technologies with geospatial processing tools.

Frontend

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Three.js
  • React Three Fiber

Backend

  • Python
  • FastAPI

Geospatial Processing

  • Rasterio
  • GDAL
  • GeoPandas
  • NumPy

Navigation & Algorithms

  • A* Search Algorithm
  • Cost Grid
  • Terrain-Based Route Optimization

System Architecture

The frontend provides the interactive exploration experience, while the backend handles geospatial processing, terrain analysis, and route calculation.

The system is designed to connect scientific raster datasets with interactive visualization and navigation services.

What Makes TAREEQ Different?

VYRA is not just another planetary visualization tool.

Its main idea is to connect scientific understanding with practical exploration.

Instead of simply displaying the Martian surface, VYRA brings together:

  • Immersive 3D terrain exploration.
  • Multiple scientific geospatial layers.
  • Interactive destination selection.
  • Algorithm-based route planning.
  • Comparison of different navigation strategies.

By combining these capabilities, VYRA creates a unified environment where users can explore, understand, and plan journeys across selected regions of Mars.

From observing the Martian surface to making informed navigation decisions.

Future Development

VYRA is designed with room for future expansion beyond its initial regional MVP.

Potential future improvements include:

  • MediaPipe-based hand tracking for touchless exploration.
  • More immersive interaction with the 3D Martian environment.
  • Integration of additional Martian regions and scientific datasets.
  • More advanced terrain hazard analysis.
  • Expanded mission planning capabilities.
  • Improved scientific-interest identification and visualization.

Our long-term vision is to develop VYRA into a more comprehensive interactive environment for planetary exploration and mission planning.
